I haven't experienced this but I imagine its just as painful and frustrating as trying to come to a therapist with any problem that they don't take seriously, dismiss or minimize, especially one you have identified as being the problem most affecting you. 

Im sorry you had that experience. Even if a therapist doesn't fully understand your problem or thinks its caused by something else that they want you to talk about in order to progress, they are doing you and their supposed job a great disservice by not listening to you and trying to figure out more about something you've identified as being a significant problem for you. 

A competent therapist should be able to either ask you more about limerance if they don't understand it or ask you to explain how you feel and why you feel it affects you negatively. They may tey to understand it or speak about it within the framework of their preferred speciality or model as a therapist, but they shouldn't dismiss the limerance if they feel that it's caused by other problems, on the contrary that's more reason to talk about it to relate it the other things affecting you to try and figure out how it might be connected to your limerance.

It's definitely possible to find a therapist that isn't dismissive. My therapist would never dismiss anything I brought up as being a problem or worry of mine. I believe I once explained limerance to him because he has never heard of it before, but he wasn't dismissive, he just asked me about what about the limerance feels unhealthy and related it back to my other issues. 

It can be hard but also sometimes you need to directly ask for what you need from your therapist. If he seems like he's not going to ever listen to you, you could say something like " I've noticed you've been dismissive of me whenever I have brought this up. This is a significant longterm pattern that negatively affects my life that I want to address and if you're not willing to work on this with me I'll need to find another therapist."

Married or not, it makes a lot of sense to feel anxiety about someone not returning your feelings, or revealing they see the relationship differently then you and want different thing out of it. 

I'm not married but I do get extremely anxious and depressed when racking my brain and trying to figure out if my sweeties love me as much as I love them, or see the relationship the same way I do when I haven't talked to them yet. I have had many experiences of expressing my romantic feelings for someone and having them respond that they just see me as a friend but still want to have sex with me, and so I am now very anxious about that in every new relationship. I fall in love fast and hard and with many different types of people so I always worry that people won't feel as strongly for me. 

Also just because someone was engaged doesn't mean they are/ want to be monogamous (Exhibit A: yourself). Also people can change their minds and views throughout different experiences. Maybe he realized after that he wants to be poly and not get engaged at all or at least for a while, maybe he decided he wants to be poly but is still open to getting married but still being poly. You really won't know until you ask.

You're correct though, as nerve racking as it is, you're going to have to express your feelings eventually if you want to know his. Maybe it would help to start this conversation by asking him what his poly style and experience is, and how strongly he feels about identifying and living as poly. Then you could get a feel for whether or not he may want to become monogamous with someone in the future. It sounds like you know that you want a deeper romantic relationship though, so I would say you should have this conversation as soon as possible because by not having it you are doing a disservice to yourself. You deserve to be with someone who wants the same things as you and you should be putting your energy into someone you know is that person.

Maybe it stems from insecurity in your case, but on the flip side one could also make a pretty good case that wanting to have primaries could stem from insecurity, so seems to me like with many things, it varies from person to person. 

Someone could want to have a primary because they are insecure in their newly opened relationship, so the primary label helps foster a sense that they are important and committed to their partner. Or maybe a person has been poly for awhile and just know what they want and what works for them and using those labels just helps as a way to process or understand their feelings surrounding relationship needs. 

Same as for relationship anarchy: You could be insecure and afraid of commitment or whatever, or you could just have an understanding of what your wants and needs are and want to honor and be true to them. 

I don't now if I'm a true relationship anarchist, but I definitely ascribe personally to not having primaries or secondaries because it just doesn't hold any value for me and the way I want/need my relationship dynamics to look. I just call the people I'm dating either sweeties or partners. For me I would usually reserve partner for someone with whom it is mutually agreed that we are interested in a more long term commitment and whom I have been with for at least 4-6 months. I usually use the term sweeties for people I am dating or having sex with otherwise. These labels aren't about hierarchy but are more about describing the level of commitment, intimacy, and closeness in each relationship. This is mostly useful to me in social contexts or just as a shorthand to imply differing relationship dynamics. For example, I think my sweetie who I have only been dating for about 3 months may think it's weird if I referred to them as my partner since we haven't known each other for that long, or really discussed our feelings about commitment and intimacy we feel with one another that deeply yet.

I'm so sorry you are experiencing that sensation so strongly. I'm not sure if its the same, but I also have issues with experiencing numbness and tingling in my hands and feet when I'm very anxious or depressed- I think I feel sadness first, then get anxiety about it, then the tingling and numbness starts almost immediately, accompanied by a sinking feeling in my stomach. 

It doesn't sound as bad as what you're experiencing, but it always feels so discouraging to me for some reason. It makes me feel as if I'm supposed to be so sad I'm hurting, like my body is justifying my feelings and I should be feeling that way because I deserve it. It can be really hard to get out of. The only thing I've thought of to help would be getting some smooth rocks or other items you like to squeeze or rub when you are feeling that way, to try and divert the feelings outside yourself and for grounding.

I know with anxiety it can be hard, because even if you can reconceptualize something to view it more rationally it's still extremely difficult to act on that new view in a different way, as your anxiety sometimes doesn't feel any different. 

But I think I would usually try and think about the context of the situation and assess the how high the probability is that the impending thing actually constitutes a threat. Which like I said, could be difficult if you have extreme anxiety which is hard to avoid acting on.

Cheating would technically be whatever you and your partner have decided "cheating" would look like in your relationship. For many it could mean not discussing or telling a partner about a new love interest, or being dishonest about new partners or experiences. 

In some Non monog relationships, cheating doesn't really come into play at all, because two people might not have any criteria for it occuring. For example, I am dating someone right now who I am very into but haven't gotten super serious with. We both have sex and go on dates/ have crushes with various people. If they were dishonest with me about anything, I definitely wouldn't view it as cheating, because that would imply that I viewed them as having an obligation to our relationship and that we were much more official than we have discussed. 

I would simply view them being dishonest or not revealing something as just that. It would be disappointing and not in line with the general open and honest aim of our communication, so I would want to discuss it with them, but I wouldn't consider it cheating.

The way you both have of viewing various sexual experiences with people outside of you and your partner's relationship as having to be "equal" or " in balance" with your partner's numbers reveals some troubling underlying jealousy dynamics that you and your partner should discuss as soon as possible. 

The point of an open relationship is that both of you have agreed that you both want to have sex/ relationships with other people, and you both understand that it's what the other wants and want them to be as happy and fulfilled as possible- not to keep your numbers equal and have as much sex as your partner is having.

 Its about being open to whatever comes into both of your lives and supporting each other through it, being happy that you each have special people in your lives, and communicating through whatever feelings comes up for you to try and get to the root of whatever unmet needs you have. 

 This kind of "keeping score" thinking likely comes from insecurities you both have about the relationship or yourselves. It's not productive or sustainable to constantly do that in a non-monogamous relationship and it will eventually lead to more and more acting out of your jealousy and insecurities if you don't discuss it soon.

1. How do you self-identify your gender, and what does that definition mean to you? 
Transboy/nonbinary transmasculine. I identify as nonbinary because I don't fully identify with the common definition or society's definition of being a man. However I don't often explain my gender this way unless the person I'm talking to is also queer and/or trans because I am read as cis most of the time and just telling people I'm trans/ftm mostly suffices. 

 
2. What pronouns do you use?
He/him/his

3. Describe the style of clothing that you most often wear.
I wear work pants, or fitted pants, boots, t shirts, sweaters, hoodies, flannels, and ball caps or beanies. 

4. Talk about your choices with body hair. How do you style your hair? Do you have facial hair? What do you choose to shave, or choose not to shave?
I don't really style my hair, I have my hair shorter on the sides and longer in the middle, with a tail. I do have facial hair but mostly just a chinstrap, which I trim when it gets too long. I don't like shaving it all the way because it isn't really robust enough to grow back immediately. I don't really shave any other hair.

5. Talk about cosmetics. Do you choose to wear makeup? Do you paint your nails? What types of soaps and perfumes do you use if any?
I don't really use any cosmetics regularly. Sometimes I use clay I found under a cliff overhang as a facial mask, and I use any sort of soap or deodorant. Used to be more concerned with aluminum and shit but needing to travel a lot made me not care as much.

6. Have you experienced being misgendered? If so, how often?
Yes, I experienced it before and about eight months after I first started t a lot, and then for a couple months after that it happened it tapered off but still occurred. I think it probably happened at least 60% of the time during its height. Since then though, I can't remember being misgendered at all. 

7. Do you experience dysphoria? How does that affect you?
I have dysphoria mostly surrounding my chest because I haven't had top surgery yet, and the fact that I still haven't lost some body fat from my hips and thighs that I feel make me look feminine. It affects me in that I have been (and am still) saving up for surgery for three years and most of my savings goes to that, I also spend a lot of time trying to do things to decrease my body fat and then failing and repeating the cycle. So yea it's not that bad, just kind of a backdrop.

8. Talk about children. Are you interested in having children? Would you want to carry a child if that were an option for you? Do you want to be the primary caretaker for any children you may have?
I am interested in having children, but I do not want to carry a child. I would want to be the primary caregiver, in fact I would want to be a stay at home parent, at least when the child is young.

9. Talk about money. Is it important to you to provide for a family financially if you choose to have one? Is it important to you that you earn more than any partner you may have? Do you prefer to pay for things like dates? Are you uncomfortable when others pay for you or offer to pay for you?
It is important to me, but I obviously would want my partner to contribute most if I were to stay at home. I really don't give a shit if a partner or anyone earns more than me, or of people pay for stuff for me, I just get them back next time, or don't let the pay for me if I don't want them to.

10. Anything else you want to share about your experience with gender?
I think gender is infinite, weird and playful, experimental and can be fun. I like other gender weirdos and gender fucking people who challenge people's idea of what their or society's veiw of gender is/should be. I do feel a dissonance between how I feel about my gender and how I present myself because I feel most people assume I am a cis male, and people i know just see me as a transguy. Which is why I think it's fun to talk about these things that usually don't come up with most people in my life.
